title: The Fermi Paradox: Why We Might Be Alone in the Galaxy
narration: Three hundred million Earth-like planets in our galaxy. And yet, where is everybody? The Fermi Paradox asks: Where is everybody? Attributed to physicist Enrico Fermi.
visual_goal: A swirling Milky Way galaxy with 300 million tiny glowing dots representing Earth-like planets. The camera zooms into one dot, then cuts to a silent, empty cityscape at night.

title: The Great Silence
narration: Over sixty years of listening with SETI, no confirmed technosignals detected to date. The Wow! Signal, detected in nineteen seventy-seven by the Big Ear Radio Observatory, remains unexplained.
visual_goal: A vintage radio telescope dish scanning the sky. The screen flashes with the Wow! Signal waveform, then cuts to static.

title: The Great Filter
narration: Over fifty proposed resolutions to the Fermi Paradox. One terrifying thought: Are we next?
visual_goal: A split screen: one side shows a lush, thriving Earth; the other, a barren, lifeless planet. The camera zooms into a ticking clock.

title: The James Webb Revelation
narration: JWST can detect potential biosignatures, such as oxygen, in exoplanet atmospheres, but abiotic processes may also produce such signatures. A single whiff of oxygen. Life? Or just the universe playing tricks?
visual_goal: A close-up of the James Webb Space Telescope. Its lens zooms into an exoplanet’s atmosphere, revealing spectral lines of oxygen and methane.

title: The Final Answer
narration: The universe is silent. We might be alone. Or the silence *is* the answer.
visual_goal: A lone astronaut floats in space, looking at a distant galaxy. The camera pulls back to reveal the vast emptiness of the cosmos.
